name: message
title: Message
purpose: One row of an agent transcript: the start of the session, a prompt, the agent's text, a question to the reader, a tool call, its result, an answered permission request, a denial, an error, usage or the end of a turn.
whenToUse: For each event of an agent's turn, as a list item in the transcript's ol or ul, oldest first.
To show what a tool was asked to do and what it returned, in mono, at phone width.
whenNotToUse: For a request that still waits for the reader's answer. Use an approval, which carries Allow and Decline.
For the note that the agent is still working. Use streaming as the last row.
For a message about the app itself, such as a lost connection. Use an alert or a banner.

variants.name: agent
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. Text the agent wrote. Label it with the agent's name.

variants.name: session-start
variants.use: A quiet first row saying that the session started, and where: the branch, the directory, the agent. Label it Session.

variants.name: user
variants.use: A prompt the reader sent. Label it You.

variants.name: question
variants.use: A question the agent asks the reader, when the run waits on the answer. Label it Question, waiting on you, and once it is answered label it Question and show the answer as the next user row. A request for permission to run something is not a question: use an approval.

variants.name: tool-call
variants.use: A tool the agent ran, written as what it did and not as raw JSON: the tool name in gw-message__tool, then the command or the target in mono in gw-message__command, then optionally one plain sentence saying why in gw-message__body, taken from the call's description when it has one. Keep the full arguments behind a details element whose summary reads Show the full arguments, or, when the row has no sentence, whose summary keeps the label, the tool name and a short command.

variants.name: tool-result
variants.use: What a tool returned. Show the first lines, and put the rest in a details element whose summary reads Show full output.

variants.name: decision
variants.use: A permission request that was resolved. The label says how, in words beside an icon from the sprite in gw-message__icon: Allowed with check, Declined with x, Pre-approved with circle-check for a command on the task's approved list, or Allowed by a standing permission with circle-check. Then the tool and the command, then one sentence saying by whom and when: who allowed or declined it and their note, who set the approved list, or who granted the standing permission. For the last two, say that nobody was asked.

variants.name: denied
variants.use: A call the permission rules refused without asking. Say what was not run and why. For a request a person declined, use the decision row.

variants.name: error
variants.use: Something that failed: a tool that crashed, a lost connection, a limit reached. Say what failed, what state the work is in and what to do next. It is not for a refused call, which is the denied row.

variants.name: usage
variants.use: A quiet line of figures for the turn, such as tokens and duration.

variants.name: turn-end
variants.use: A quiet closing row under a rule, saying that the turn finished and how: completed, stopped or ended with an error.

accessibility: Each row is an li in an ol or ul. Put role="log" and an accessible name on the list when rows are added while the reader watches, so new rows are announced.

Every row starts with gw-message__label, which says the kind in words: Session, You, Claude Code, Question, Tool call, Tool result, Allowed, Declined, Pre-approved, Allowed by a standing permission, Denied, Error, Usage, End. The kind is never the colour or an icon alone. The icons of the denied and error rows are drawn by the stylesheet, and the icon of an answered request is an svg with gw-message__icon and aria-hidden="true" inside the label.
A question row that waits says so in its label, Question, waiting on you. Once it is answered the label reads Question alone.
Write transcript text as text, never as markup, and write out characters that cannot be seen.

Collapsed arguments and long output use a native details element, with no script. Its summary holds text that says what is inside. Enter and Space open and close it, and its pointer target is 44px tall.
When output is cut short, the lines after the preview go in the details element, so opened text continues where the preview stopped.
The app sets nothing but the open attribute, which the browser manages.
